# Bug register

_Generated from `docs/bugs/bugs.json` with AmiWind v0.0.64-dev4._

The single list of every AmiWind bug and its current status. How tracking
works, the report template and the rules: [bug tracking](bugs/README.md).
Dated events are in the [journal](BUG_JOURNAL.md); full reports are in
[docs/bugs](bugs/README.md). CHIM engine bugs by part, with the build each was found
in: [CHIM Engine tracker](bugs/CHIM_TRACKER.md).

## Fix index

Generated from [`docs/bugs/bugs.json`](bugs/bugs.json): do not edit this table
by hand. Change the JSON (or use `tools/bug_register.py add` / `set`), then run
`tools/bug_register.py render`. A test fails if the two disagree.

`fixed` means a correction shipped in the named version with supporting
verification; candidates and mitigations stay `open`. `closed` means not a bug,
a duplicate or superseded (the status says which).

Three causes, each measured with the per-frame file counter: the player's assembled body (21 parts loaded in one frame, each opened three times), the compiled scripts' journal names (a 16 KB buffer refilled twice per topic, 6.9 s), and the actor rows (a binary search on disk with a 16 KB buffer, about 1 s). Fixed in v0.0.59: the body's parts load over several frames and stay in memory (aw_player_cache 1, 281 KB), a file is opened once instead of three times, the journal names are read in one pass, the actor rows use a small buffer and recent finds are kept. The first play frame is now about 1.0 s (server 0.36 s, screen 0.38 s); the parts are no longer reloaded later in play, and wearing a cuirass loads one part in 50 ms. Still open: the first frame is above 0.5 s; the parts are not yet one packed file; CHIM chunks (.ccs) are still opened more than once in the load frame. |

| [AUDIO-LOAD-29](bugs/AUDIO-LOAD-29.md) | OST crackles under heavy loading | high | v0.0.29-rc1 | open | - | - | - | Fixed in source on v0.0.52-dev (25 October 2026), not built yet: the first load after the intro movie ran the music dry 1-3 times (v0.0.51-dev3 and the final: 0 late, every other load 0 dry). Cause: the music stream reads its next 16 KiB block only from the frame loop (CDAudio_Update) or as the painter's emergency fill; a load holds the frame loop, and the track restarted after the movie with an empty buffer. Now every load-time mixer update (snd_dma.c S_Update_) also pumps the stream's reads (aw_music.c AW_MusicLoadPump, never waits; not under the movie); tests: music_player_test loadpump, aga_loading_audio_test. To verify: the audio smoke of the next dev build, the first load 0 dry, and the maintainer's WinUAE listen. Measured again (FS-UAE, 32 MB, the dev2 image with the gate 3891 engine, the same five loads): longest gaps 58 (first load, outside a 4,893 ms movie), 43, 52, 115 (Akulakhan's Chamber, world model to entities) and 49 ms, 0 late. | [BUILD-CUTOFF-WHOLE-ANCESTOR-51](bugs/BUILD-CUTOFF-WHOLE-ANCESTOR-51.md) | An interior light change reran exterior stages: the reuse cutoff refuses a stage when any earlier stage's whole output differs, not the files it reads | medium | v0.0.51-dev3 (2026_10_25_v0.0.51-dev3_dev3_f700a7bd) | open | - | - | - | Open (25 October 2026): v0.0.51-dev3 changed only tools/interior_lighting.py (and the engine). The read trace records checkout reads only, never run-folder reads, so the cutoff cannot narrow to what a stage opened. | [BUILD-DISK-NEED-UNKNOWN-52](bugs/BUILD-DISK-NEED-UNKNOWN-52.md) | A public build can die halfway when the disk fills: the only space check runs once at the start, against a fixed 20 GiB, not what the release really takes | high | v0.0.50 (2026_10_25_v0.0.51_final_d74cc652) | open | - | - | - | Reported by a tester (passed on by the maintainer, 2026-10-26): their v0.0.50 build from the public repository stopped when the disk ran out; the free-space check runs only before the first stage and asks a fixed 20 GiB (AMIWIND_MIN_FREE_GIB), however much the build needs. The maintainer: a gate check from the start, compared with the release s own build size, automatically against the previous known good build with about 20 % extra. Fix: every passing build records its measured full-build footprint (peak bytes of the workspace, the caches and the scratch, per file system); the release ships the last known good build s figure in the repository; before any stage the preflight asks for that figure plus 20 % on each file system and stops with the numbers when it is short; each stage checks its own last measured bytes plus 20 % before it starts; a gate test fails when the shipped footprint is missing or older than the release. The maintainer (2026-10-26 15:20 +0200 / 2026-10-26 13:20 UTC): the margin about 30 % or more, depending on the dependencies; the need counts everything a fresh build takes, not only the workspace: the builder images (about 2.2 GB each), the Morrowind game data copied into the Docker volume, the caches, the storage pool and the scratch. Measured 2026-10-26: the build runs alone take 19 GB (v0.0.51 final) and 16 GB (v0.0.52-dev3), on top of the shared pool and caches. Fix written (2026-10-26 19:45 +0200 / 2026-10-26 17:45 UTC, v0.0.53 builder, branch v0.0.53-disk): tools/disk_need.py. The check runs first in every image build (tools/build.py right after the options are read: build.sh, build.cmd and the build inside Docker), before the builder image is built (tools/build_docker.py, where Docker storage is visible from the host) and before the game data is copied into a volume (tools/run_docker.py, checked inside the image); and before each stage against that stage's own last figure (tools/build_profile.py start). The need per file system: the last known good build's figure (the larger of the shipped config/disk-footprint.json and this workspace's newest passing build) plus disk_margin_percent (30), less the cache and pool when the workspace already holds a passing build's, the workspace never below min_free_gib (35); both in config/build-defaults.json as machine settings that key no stage (tools/build_cache.py keys that file without them; AMIWIND_MIN_FREE_GIB, AMIWIND_DISK_MARGIN_PERCENT and AMIWIND_DISK_WATCH were keyed environment before: now ignored), also --min-free-gib and --disk-margin-percent. Every passing build writes RUN/disk-footprint.json (run folder bytes, scratch peak from the free space sampled every 5 s, cache and pool growth, game data, per-stage peak growth); tools/disk_need.py ship RUN puts it into the repository. First figure, measured read-only on the build volume: the v0.0.52 final's run folder 15.47 GiB (dev3 the same), storage pool objects written in the v0.0.52 cycle 28.84 GiB (an over-count), game data 1.79 GiB, builder image 2.0 GiB: a fresh native build needs about 58 GiB, Docker about 63 GiB. Gate tests: tests/test_disk_need.py (no stage re-keyed by the settings, a stage stops before it starts, a passing build writes its figure, the shipped figure exists and is not older than the release, the guides state the need). Open until a build writes the first measured figure with stage figures. Gate 4048 (2026-10-26 20:14 +0200 / 2026-10-26 18:14 UTC) stopped on tests/test_run_docker (a missing --input-volume must be refused before any Docker run): the volume check now runs right before the game data copy when there is one, otherwise right after the input checks and before the build container is made. |

| BUILD-KEY-MESH-TABLE-WHOLE-54 | A per-mesh measured table is keyed whole: one new row of collision-standing-room.json re-keyed every room, resident and model unit | high | v0.0.54-dev2 (2026_10_28_v0.0.54-dev2_full-dev2-try2_dea1bef) | open | - | - | - | Partly fixed in v0.0.55-dev1 (28 October 2026): the unit caches key the per-mesh measured tables by the rows each unit read (tools/mesh_tables.py, tests/test_mesh_table_keys.py), so one new row re-keys only that mesh's units. | BUILD-KEY-UNIT-RESTORED-CODE-52 | A stage whose last real run restored its units from a cache was reused after the code those units come from changed: chim-room-batches kept actor models of the old animation tables | high | v0.0.52-dev1 (2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev1_dev1-try11_28046c31) | open | - | - | - | Found 2026-10-26 06:29 +0200 / 2026-10-26 04:29 UTC in dev1-try11 (28046c31, reusing try10): the image step stopped on Room batches collide with the image: progs/a_*.mdl and .tag staged with other bytes. chim-room-batches was reused (fingerprint fdd5a1e1, unchanged) although 28046c31 changed tools/skeletal_actor.py and tools/npc_anim.py, which bake its residents (prepare_area.populate): both files are in its closure, but the key covers only the functions its last real run called, and that run restored its residents from the resident unit cache, so the changed table functions (game_table, table_choice, table_groups) were never called and are not in the key. The area stage, which baked, rebuilt with the new tables; the two wrote the same actor names with different bytes. Worked around in dev1-try12 with --rebuild-stage chim-room-batches. Fix: a unit restored from a cache counts the code its unit key covers as called (the unit cache environment digest becomes a stage input), or a stage that restores units keeps the whole module closure of the code that makes them. Fixed in source (2026-10-26 07:48 +0200 / 2026-10-26 05:48 UTC): a pass or unit cache keeps the trace lines of the code its key covers (pass_cache.covered_lines: @path TAB unit for each function its key reaches, =path for a file it keys whole) and on its first hit in a process appends them to the stage trace (note_covered); build_cache.used_record keys an = file whole, also when some of its code ran ('=' joins TRACE_MARKS). A stage that takes its residents from the resident unit cache now has the table code in its narrowed key. Tests: test_pass_cache (a hit writes what the key covers, once), test_build_cache (a file a cache keyed counts whole). To confirm: the next dev build after a table-code change rebuilds chim-room-batches without --rebuild-stage. |

| BUILD-ORDERED-MAP-SCAN-51 | The pool map that hands results back in input order scans every held future on each turn: the main process works O(n squared) while large maps run | medium | v0.0.51-dev1 | open | - | - | - | Open (25 October 2026): found profiling the main process of a cached CHIM validation on the v0.0.51-dev1 world (22 workers): ordered_map 8.2 s of its own, Future.done 5.2 million calls (4 s), the _running count 3.8 million (3.5 s). With a cost every item is submitted largest first, so pending holds every result not yet handed back (up to all 1351); each loop turn counts the running ones over all of pending (_running) and builds the wait list over all of pending. Repair: count and wait only on the submitted-and-running set (at most the limit). Not done yet: ordered_map is not a scheduling unit, so any edit re-keys every stage and per-unit cache that reaches it (the NPC gallery faces, the stair data: a build that walks stairs is barred). First make the dispatch loop a scheduling unit with a new key form (BUILD-KEY-RULE-NO-FORM-51), then repair it |

| [CHIM-BC-TREE-PYRAMID-BOX-47](bugs/CHIM-BC-TREE-PYRAMID-BOX-47.md) | Bitter Coast trees (flora_bc_tree family) look like a pyramid trunk with a flat box floating above it | medium | v0.0.47-dev1 (2026_10_21_v0.0.47-dev1_dev1-try2_4a2d42b9) | open | - | - | - | 2026-11-10, branch v0.0.64-fence2: the renderer now has a see-through face kind. The converter marks every texture whose alpha channel leaves at least 1 % of its texels under half alpha (name prefix "{", palette index 255 for its transparent texels; other textures keep their bytes and unit keys), and the engine draws those faces in a separate pass after the walls, z-tested, skipping index 255 (aw_fence, dbg fence; off by default until a measured A/B on the next full build decides). Proof pending: the cobweb in Andrano Ancestral Tomb and a hanging growth outdoors with the switch off and on. Bitter Coast crowns that use see-through textures are covered by the same pass; their geometry is unchanged here. Earlier: Open: cause unknown; proposed fix direction: crossed vertical planes with the tree's outline (alpha kept), angle impostors as the alternative; A/B first, nothing built. Seen again in v0.0.62-dev1 (PERSISTING): Bitter Coast trees with fungi growing on them are drawn as a distorted stand-in, a dome-like shape at flora_bc_tree_08, taken from its collision-only model, so the bracket fungus (Hypha Facia) beside it floats in the air (FUNGI-FLOATING-62; the earlier floating-tree fix BC-TREE-FLOATING-60 covered trees that did not reach the ground, a different fault). Decided direction: (1) a tree whose parts can be picked or touched gets a very low-polygon solid trunk with measured dimensions, no part thinner than half its original width and no new gaps (the method in the mesh reduction notes, MESH-REDUCTION-SEAMS-62); (2) purely decorative foliage can be transparent planes or sprites; (3) fungi are seated on the trunk surface. |

| [CHIM-ROOM-HEART-CHAMBER-LOAD-50](bugs/CHIM-ROOM-HEART-CHAMBER-LOAD-50.md) | Entering Akulakhan s Chamber (the Heart Chamber) ends the game: a model of its room store does not load, and the engine stops with Host_Error instead of refusing at the door | critical | v0.0.50 (2026_10_24_v0.0.50_final_ffb87463) | open | - | - | - | Cause found and fixed in source on v0.0.51-dev (24 October 2026), not shipped at the time of writing: 32 MB got no automatic cache bank (CHIM-AUTO-BANK-CLIFF-51), so the room's 10.1 MiB of models did not fit. With the repaired engine dbg tp heartchamber at 32 MB loads the room in play (365 placements, 135 models, 5.0 s). Open part: a room that cannot load during play still stops at the console instead of refusing at the door PERSISTING in v0.0.52-dev2 (2026-10-26 11:18 +0200 / 2026-10-26 09:18 UTC, FS-UAE JIT, 32 MB, image 2026_10_26_v0.0.52-dev2_dev2_3715e8c4). Seyda Neen, then Balmora (dbg cam recall bm3), then dbg tp heartchamber ended in Host_Error: CHIM room map maps/rifa4ef181ed.chim: its room record or models cannot be loaded. The room found 2 MiB of the free Fast RAM for its models (and 1994 KiB of the Hunk) and a model of the store could not be loaded. Afterwards: Memory now 4795 KiB free, largest block 4492 KiB. Loaded as the first map it works: 4 MiB taken, Memory now 1291 KiB free, largest block 1177 KiB, zone 1476 KiB free. The difference was the skeletal session memory held since the town: the animation tables and the large pose cache, 1589 KiB. Fixed in 2d49fb88 (gate 4032): before Chim_RoomGrow measures the free Fast RAM, the engine flushes its skeletal models from the model cache and gives back the tables and the large pose cache, all made again on demand (aw_skel_release.c). Checked on a play copy of the dev2 image with the 2d49fb88 engine swapped in: the same route loads the chamber (1589 KiB given back first, 3 MiB of Fast RAM and 1994 KiB of the Hunk taken, room 148 models 18129 KiB loaded in 2701 ms). Afterwards Memory now is 2200 KiB free, largest block 2058 KiB; the zone has 420 KiB free, largest run 417 KiB. The Heart's structure and a figure before it are in view. Still open at 32 MB: 2 model loads fail both after the town and as the first map (zone failed requests, the last 250624 bytes after the town, 60112 as the first map); at 64 MB 0 fail. Which models these are (Dagoth Ur's full model and the Heart's actor are the suspects, outside the build gate's count) is not identified yet. Stills: clips/v0.0.52 akulakhan_chamber_32mb_after_balmora, 32mb_first_map, 64mb_after_balmora. 2026-10-26 12:53 +0200 / 2026-10-26 10:53 UTC: named and fixed (v0.0.52, gate 4034). The two failed loads at 32 MB were not models left out: zone failed: model 1639 (x/ex_dwrv_enter00, a Dwemer entrance of the room, 250,580 bytes) and model 4991 (i/in_akulacave00 tile 5,8, 147,092 bytes) are the requests that made the room grow (try 1 full, the free Fast RAM bank; try 2 full, the Hunk rest; try 3 loaded): every model was in place (room: 148 models, 18,129 KiB; zone used = the gate's need), neither Dagoth Ur (an actor model in Quake's cache, not the zone) nor the Heart. The console now says so (room: loaded whole on try 3; it grew 2 times, each after a request the full zone refused). The real shortfall was the margin: after Balmora the room bank was 3 MiB (zone 420 KiB free) because the tables given back do not join the largest block and the bank was cut to whole MiB. Fixed: the room bank in 64 KiB steps (CHIM_ROOM_GRAIN); a registry of re-makeable session memory (aw_fastrelease.c AW_FastReleaseRegister/AW_FastReleaseAll, 8 releasers, one console line each with free and largest block before and after) called before the CHIM cache banks at start-up, -chimcache and a room's growth (never per frame), the skeletal tables and posed frames its first releaser; a console line of the free Fast RAM at the room step. Measured at 32 MB after Balmora (FS-UAE, dev2 image, new engine): given back 1,589 KiB, free 4,696 -> 6,286 KiB, largest 4,488 -> 5,512 KiB, bank 3,456 KiB (was 3,072), zone 804 KiB free (was 420), Memory now 1,814 KiB free, largest 1,671. The room heap gate counts the worse route now (engine_limits MEASURED_ROOM 5,512 KiB: bank 3,456 KiB; the chamber needs 19,093,616 of 19,968,800, its walk leaves 848 KiB, measured 804) and the actors: the animation tables their skeletal models name and the pose cache must fit what the room bank leaves (CHIM_ROOM_KEEP 2 MiB), else the gate fails (the chamber: humanoid table 579,816 + pose cache 393,984 = 990,188 bytes). Tests: tests/test_fast_release.py (native registry with stubs, call sites, every MEMF_LARGEST sizing listed), aga_chim_world_test roomgrow, test_chim_room_heap; m68k 4 variants clean. 2026-10-26 13:02 +0200 / 2026-10-26 11:02 UTC: committed 9741c99c (gate 4034 passed, 5,913 tests); in-game check in the dev3 image. |

| [CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43](bugs/CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43.md) | Travelling from Seyda Neen to Balmora sometimes hangs on the Loading screen (boot smoke, 2 of about 5 runs) | high | v0.0.43-dev1 (2026_10_17_v0.0.43-dev1_full-batch2_7ac15b1) | open | - | - | - | Open. Cause not yet shown in a capture (review of all reports, 9 November 2026): the 36 reports are not one mechanism; the examined stops show the processor idle and the game waiting for the reply to an ordinary file call that never comes. No memory error and no disk geometry error is indicated (heap marks identical after every unload). Hypotheses in order of fit: (1) a completion notification lost inside the emulator between its host threads and the emulated machine (a shared interrupt-request word written without atomic operations: in the emulator's published 3.1.66 source it is a volatile, not atomic, word that several parts read, change and write back; whether that happens in a hang is not yet shown); (2) the lost request belongs to the test tooling's remote-console folder (a directory drive polled twice a second), not to the game disk, which would mean players are not affected; (3) an interrupt lost inside the emulated machine (weak). Next: every stop examined before the retry, naming the pending request's handler; a memory and load trace after every load; the route with the remote console off against on; then a capture with the emulator's threads stopped. No read timeouts in the game until then: a late reply would land in a reused buffer. |

| CHIM-STORE-ONE-AT-A-TIME-64 | The engine streams one CHIM store at a time, so frames of a second store cannot sit beside the first in the open world | high | v0.0.64-dev2 (2026_11_10_v0.0.64-dev2_miniwind-solstheim) | open | - | - | - | Open. Solstheim belongs to the same exterior world as Vvardenfell, on the same cell grid, north-west of it, with open sea between. Today a CHIM map names its store and Chim_StoreSelect refuses to change store while a CHIM map runs; model, texture and file ids belong to one store. A Solstheim frame kept in its own store (chimsol, the test image) therefore loads only as a separate map, not streamed next to the Vvardenfell frames. Way out without re-keying the base world: one exterior index whose base part is byte-identical and whose Solstheim frames, models and textures are appended after the base ids (an image-side merge of the two indexes), or an engine that keeps both indexes and looks a frame up by its cell in either. |

Morrowind's land texture layer is 16 x 16 squares per cell and blends neighbouring squares; ours draws one texture per square with hard edges. Planned A/B, first option the maintainer's (20:04): (d) DIAGONAL SPLITS: where a square's texture meets a different texture on two adjacent sides (a corner of a stair-step edge), split that square along its diagonal into two triangles, each with one texture, so stair-steps become 45-degree edges (marching-squares over the texture grid; about one extra face per split square, no new textures). Then, if needed: (a) baked transition textures for the edge pairs that occur, (b) a dithered edge band baked into the surfaces, (c) finer squares along roads. Measured in faces, memory and frame time; OpenMW at the same pose. |

OpenMW 0.51 mwclass/npc.cpp getArmorRating adds the Shield effect's magnitude to the armour rating, and a blow landing on an actor is reduced by that rating. The player's combat sheet (aw_combat.c AW_CombatPlayerSheet, aw_inventory.c inv_combat) holds the worn pieces and the unarmored rating only, so a Shield changes nothing in a fight; the inventory window's rating (AW_CombatPlayerArmorRating) already adds it. Planned: the same magnitude added where a blow on the player is reduced, read at the blow (the effect can start and end during a fight). |

| ENGINE-RTG-SLOW-PATH-52 | With a graphics card installed the engine picks an RTG screen, then draws it through the slow generic path: the direct CyberGraphX copy is switched off | medium | v0.0.50 (2026_10_25_v0.0.51_final_d74cc652) | open | - | - | - | From a tester s minimal RTG patch (passed on by the maintainer, 2026-10-26; private copy, not merged): VID_Init opens cybergraphics.library and, when it is there, asks BestCModeIDTags for an RTG mode, so is_cyber_mode is set; VID_Update then sends the frame through WritePixelArray8 (a one-row planar bitmap per rect) because the direct WritePixelArray RECTFMT_LUT8 call is inside #if 0, and that disabled call passed rects->width as the source modulo where the buffer row (vid.rowbytes) is right. The bootcheck also refuses a machine without AGA. Not confirmed on our side yet: needs the virtual graphics card (UAEgfx) with Picasso96 on the emulated Amiga. Scope (roadmap, RTG beside AGA): AGA stays the default where AGA exists; RTG when there is no AGA or when chosen; the upload from Fast RAM (not drawing into card memory) is the design the roadmap measures first. |

| EQUIP-SHARDAXE-REFUSED-61 | Equipping the iron shardaxe is refused while the iron longsword can be equipped | low | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61 (tracker PLAYER-GEAR-VISUAL-59). With one iron shardaxe carried, equip is refused ("Diagnostic inventory equip refused."), while the iron longsword is equipped at once. Cause: the inventory catalogue marks a weapon or shield as one the engine can equip only when it has no enchantment at all, and the iron shardaxe carries a Cast When Strikes enchantment. The same rule refused 191 weapons with Cast When Strikes, 59 with Cast When Used and 20 shields with Cast When Used in the v0.0.61-dev1 catalogue. Fix on the v0.0.61 line (the catalogue step, tools/prepare_inventory.py): a weapon or shield whose enchantment does nothing while it is merely held (Cast When Strikes, Cast When Used) is equipped as any other; only a worn item's Constant Effect enchantment is an active effect (OpenMW 0.51), and those stay refused until constant effects are applied. The strike effect itself is not cast yet: WEAPON-STRIKE-ENCHANT-NOT-CAST-61. Test tests/test_inventory_assets.py. Checked in game on a Seyda Neen MiniWind image built from the fix (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast): the iron shardaxe is equipped at once, held in the right hand, drawn in first person and in third person, and unequipped again. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build. |

| FOCUS-BOX-TWO-AT-ONCE-59 | Two item boxes at once: the box of the item aimed at before stays while the next item's box is drawn below the view | low | v0.0.59-dev5 (v0.0.59-tray 9014fc8f) | open | - | - | - | Open. | FOCUS-NPC-OVERRIDES-ITEM-62 | Trying to take an item near a character talks to the character instead: the nearby character overrides the item under the crosshair | high | v0.0.62-dev1 | open | - | - | - | Open. Seen three times in v0.0.62-dev1: the candle beside Sellus Gravius in the Census and Excise Office (the use key talks to him), the bracket fungi on the Bitter Coast trees with a character near (cannot be picked), and Tarhiel's journal beside his body (the use key searches the body; the journal cannot be taken or read). Cause: the use key asked the actor test first, and any actor whose box the view ray met within 72 units took the key wherever the item lay on that ray; a body's search came before every item; and an actor's own row in the placed list (at his feet) could hide an item near the crosshair. Expected, as in the reference engine: activation takes the nearest object along the view ray within the activation distance, never the nearest character. Fixed on the focus branch for v0.0.62: an item, container or plant the ray meets before the actor, or inside his box (coarser than his body: a standing actor's reach, a body lying on the floor), takes the use; an actor wholly in front of the item still takes it; actors' rows no longer take part in the item aim. A rules test checks it by number (a candle 35 ahead with a man at 50..70: the candle; a journal inside a lying body's box: the journal; an item behind him at 80: the talk), and aw_placed aim prints the choice. Waiting for an in-game check. Related: FOCUS-REACH-ITEM-ORIGIN-58, FOCUS-BOX-UNDRAWN-ITEMS-58, CENSUS-INTRO-SCRIPTS-62, HARVEST-SEYDA-TREE-SPRITE-BLOCKS-PICK-47. Tracker FOCUS-NPC-OVERRIDES-ITEM-62. |
| FOCUS-REACH-ITEM-ORIGIN-58 | The focus box measures the reach to an item's origin, not to its nearer surface as the original does | low | v0.0.58-dev3 (2026_11_01_v0.0.58-dev3_full-v0.0.58-test_6679573) | open | - | - | - | Open: the reach itself is right (GMST iMaxActivateDist 192 game units, 48 map units at the quarter scale, the same number OpenMW 0.51 uses). OpenMW measures from the camera to the ray's first hit on the item's drawn mesh; the engine measures from the eye to the item's origin, so an item is reached up to half its size later (the registration paper showed no box at 46 units). Repair: store each item's half size in the focus table and measure to the nearer side. |

| [GODMODE-COMBAT-DAMAGE-61](bugs/GODMODE-COMBAT-DAMAGE-61.md) | With god mode on, a fight's blows still take the player's health and kill the player | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Checked in part on the v0.0.61-dev2 image on 6 November 2026 at 32 MB Fast: with god mode on, the Samarys ancestor ghost's blows that hit took 0.0 health (three hits), and with it off the same blows took 1.0 to 3.7 health each. Not yet checked: god mode kept across a map load (fact 2 below). Before: Open, v0.0.61; corrected 6 November 2026. Two facts: (1) the combat layer takes a blow's damage on its own fighter sheet and never reads Quake's god flag (aw_combat.c has no FL_GODMODE check), so god mode cannot stop a fight's blows; (2) Quake clears the god flag whenever the player spawns on a map (host_cmd.c), so a teleport or door that loads a map turns god mode off without a word (the original keeps it). The session that showed the player killed ("you have been killed by Guard") had set god mode before a teleport that loaded the map, so fact 2 was enough there; fact 1 is read from the code. Planned: the combat layer skips the player's damage in god mode, and god mode survives a map load. |

| IMAGE-BIGGER-THAN-ORIGINAL-62 | The game image (3,022 MB in v0.0.62) is bigger than the original game data it is made from (1.93 GB) | high | v0.0.62 (2026_11_08_v0.0.62_full-v0.0.62_1d5eda8) | open | - | - | - | Open, measured in the v0.0.62 release image: actor models about 650 MB (2,150 whole models of 242 KB, NPC-BAKED-WHOLE-DUPLICATION-33), world partition 1,123 MB, CHIM interiors 328 MB, sound 209 MB, player parts, items, bodies and hands about 175 MB, intro 131 MB. First step in progress for v0.0.63 (branch v0.0.63-shapes): the texture coordinates and triangles that actor models repeat are stored once (builder option --shared-shapes, on by default; the engine rebuilds each model byte for byte before decoding): 219 shape files for 2,588 actor models, 78.4 MB less, every model decoded byte-identically, measured read only on the v0.0.62 payload; load time on the Pi 4B and FS-UAE at 32 MB Fast not measured yet. Next: skin tiles, then the world and interiors by file kind, sound and intro against the original files, and a size budget in the build. v0.0.63-dev1 image measured (read only, tools/image_size_report.py): 3,089 MB with the shared shapes in it (3,169 MB in v0.0.62); boot payload 1,675 MB, world partition 1,123 MB; by kind: maps and CHIM world 1,499 MB, actor and other model skins 585 MB, sounds 259 MB, the rest of the models 209 MB, intro video 137 MB; whole files repeated: 6.3 MB on the boot disk, 3.2 MB in the world. Second step, skin tiles (builder option --skin-tiles, experimental, off by default): the actor skins cut into 16x16 tiles stored once (421,753 distinct of 1,693,728) in one pool of 7 chunk files, each model a table of tile numbers rebuilt byte for byte by the engine before decoding: 318,790,160 bytes less on the v0.0.63-dev1 payload, all 2,522 tiled models decoded byte-identically by the engine reader; but a skin load becomes about 78 reads (at most 167) in place of one (on a desktop machine 0.19 ms against 0.02 ms a model with the files cached), so it stays off until a build with it on shows the place-load time on the Pi 4B and FS-UAE at 32 MB Fast within 5 %. |

| [IMAGE-LAYOUT-PLAN-ACTOR-LIBRARY-48](bugs/IMAGE-LAYOUT-PLAN-ACTOR-LIBRARY-48.md) | The image step stopped at its disk layout check: the layout plan left out the actor library it installs (+145 MB on a MiniWind boot partition) | high | v0.0.48-dev2 (2026_10_22_v0.0.48-dev2_miniwind-balmora-rooms-bsp_dd768704) | open | - | - | - | PERSISTING in v0.0.48-rc1 (24 October 2026), worked around for v0.0.48: rc1-try3 stopped 43 minutes into the image step: "The staged payload no longer matches the layout plan: DW0 holds other maps than planned (211 differ ...); DW0 holds boot units not planned there (30 ...)". The payload preflight planned 2.45 GB of boot payload on 2 partitions; the CHIM room actor bake then wrote its fitted actor models inside the step and the payload reached 3.01 GB, 3 partitions (dev2 grew 2.40 -> 2.71 GB and stayed on 2). rc1 actor models are about 6-8 % bigger each than dev2 (room batches: 6,844 models, 2,727 MB against 6,938, 2,593 MB) and about 2,000 more distinct models reach the image. Worked around: a payload that only grew is laid out from the staged files (layout_plan.follows_or_grew); require_minimal and the headroom gate still decide. The real fix (v0.0.49, the maintainer asked that the size be figured out from what has been created): the room actor bake becomes its own cached stage before the image, so the plan is computed from files that exist. |

| [INLAND-SHORE-29](bugs/INLAND-SHORE-29.md) | v0.0.29-dev1: Angular/jagged inland shoreline | medium | v0.0.29-dev1 | open | - | - | deferred | Open, needs a world rebuild; plan written, no world code changed. Seen on the v0.0.61 release image: the water edge at shores and ponds runs in saw-tooth steps (Suran, cell 6,-7, and ponds and the outer coast across the map). First suspect: the reduction of the land mesh at the water edge. Plan: (1) measure first, in a container, on the stored terrain of the v0.0.62 release run: per frame, the shoreline vertices (land triangles that cross the water height) whose height or angle jump between neighbours passes a threshold, against the original LAND heights; (2) one world-wide terrain pass in the builder that moves those vertices onto the original surface at the water line, adding no triangles, with a per-area count of moved vertices and a check that the shoreline stays within a set distance of the original; never a local patch. Rebuild cost: the change re-keys the terrain of every CHIM frame, so the chim stage runs again (about 17 to 18 minutes on 24 jobs in the full v0.0.62 build fe90f8e of 8 November 2026) and the image after it; the interiors stage is not touched. To be scheduled for a dev build that re-keys the chim stage anyway (tracker COASTLINE-JAGGED-62). |

| [INTERIOR-SUNLIGHT-COLOUR-51](bugs/INTERIOR-SUNLIGHT-COLOUR-51.md) | The cell sunlight is baked as brightness only: Akulakhan's Chamber is lit grey where the original lights it red | medium | v0.0.51-dev3 (2026_10_25_v0.0.51-dev3_dev3_f700a7bd) | open | - | - | - | Open (25 October 2026): the v0.0.51-dev3 heart chamber shots (FS-UAE, 32 MB, four directions from the arrival point) show the room readable, no longer near black (INTERIOR-SUNLIGHT-UNBAKED-51), but grey-brown; the cell's sunlight is 255,140,140, a strong red, and the bake takes only its luma. The bake already gives warm lamps a warm lightstyle (WARM_STYLE, R_SurfaceWarm); a tinted style per cell sunlight colour, or the room's dominant light colour, is the candidate. Judge against the original/OpenMW at the arrival pose. Census of the three masters (25 October 2026): sunlight tinted (strongest channel at least 1.5x the weakest) in 896 of 1,335 interior cells (604 red/orange, 140 yellow, 83 green, 69 blue/purple), and in 222 of them the tinted sunlight is the main light (at least 2x the ambient luma); 630 of 676 light records are tinted (447 red/orange, 129 blue/purple, 30 green, 24 yellow), and only warm lamps get a tint today; fog tinted in 762 cells Engine side in source (2026-10-25 15:15 +0200 / 2026-10-25 13:15 UTC, gate 3915): world format 0.13 gives a CHIM placement a light tint in its record flags bits 2-4 (0 none, 1 warm = aw_light_hue, 2 red, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green, 6 cool blue-white, 7 purple); its faces are built through that tint's colour table (16 KB, made from the palette the first time a map draws the tint, r_sky.c R_BuildTints) and the surface cache keys on the tint as it does on the level (d_surf.c); aw_warm_light 0 turns tints off. Test: tests/aga_chim_placement_light_test.c (record decode 12/13, table choice, cache key) and tests/test_chim_placement_light_native.py. Next: the builder writes the tint (tools/chim/interior.py, from the cell sunlight and the dominant light colour, format 0.13), then a dev build and the heart chamber shots against the original. Builder side in source (2026-10-25 15:21 +0200 / 2026-10-25 13:21 UTC, gate 3916): tools/chim/interior.py writes CHIM rooms as world format 0.13 with a tint per placement from interior_lighting.point_colour (the same ambient, sunlight and light terms as point_light, in colour; its luma is point_light) classified by light_tint (strongest channel at least 1.4x the weakest; hue bands to the seven engine tints); the rooms receipt counts light_tints per room. Tests: tests/test_chim_interior.py LightTintTests. Next: a dev build, then the heart chamber and the census office against the original. |
| [INTERIOR-SUNLIGHT-UNBAKED-51](bugs/INTERIOR-SUNLIGHT-UNBAKED-51.md) | Interiors are baked without their cell sunlight: Akulakhan's Chamber is nearly black where the original is lit red | high | v0.0.51-dev1 (2026_10_25_v0.0.51-dev1_dev1_ec96c86d) | open | - | - | - | Fixed in source on v0.0.51-dev (25 October 2026), not built yet: the bake adds the cell sunlight as the original applies it in interiors, a directional light from one fixed direction (OpenMW interiorSunPos (-1, 45 deg, 45 deg) in radians): a face gets its luma times the cosine toward it, an actor or placed model half of it; the prison ship's judged profile (OPENING-BRIGHT-31) leaves it out. Every interior is baked again in the next dev build. Before: Open (25 October 2026): the dev1 heart chamber screenshots (FS-UAE, 32 MB) are nearly black; the maintainer: lit properly in the original. The cell AMBI holds ambient, sunlight and fog; the interior bake (tools/interior_lighting.py) uses the ambient and the placed lights and never the sunlight, which the original engine applies in interiors as a directional light. Akulakhan's Chamber: ambient 20,30,30 (luma 27), sunlight 255,140,140 (luma 174), 7 lights in a large room. Of 1,335 interior cells in the three masters 322 have sunlight luma at least twice the ambient, 85 four times, 29 eight times; the prison ship (OPENING-BRIGHT-31) has less sunlight than ambient. Repair: the sunlight term in the bake as the original applies it; every interior is baked again once |

| INVENTORY-PREVIEW-STALE-61 | The inventory character preview does not change when equipment is put on or taken off in the window | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61 (tracker INVENTORY-EQUIP-CLOTHES-PREVIEW-61). With the window open, Equip and Unequip on a row change the worn set at once, but the preview keeps an earlier picture (seen on v0.0.61-dev1: the bare body with pants, shirt and shoes worn, no cuirass 1 s and 4 s after it went on, the robe kept after it came off; 4 preview renders for 7 changes). The third-person body is right each time. Cause: the parts of a changed outfit load over several frames (at most 40 ms of loading a frame, so that a change never stalls a frame) and the body keeps the previous outfit until they are all in; the window rendered its one picture in the first frame after the change, so of the previous outfit, and kept it. Fix on the v0.0.61 line: the picture waits until the new parts are all loaded (the kept picture shown meanwhile, at most 5 s), then is rendered once, as OpenMW redraws its preview after the new parts are attached; native test tests/aga_inventory_ui_test.c. Checked in game on the v0.0.61-dev1 image with the fixed engine (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast): with the window open, the iron cuirass put on, the pants taken off, the common robe put on and the pants put on again each show in the preview 1 s and 4 s after the change, 5 renders for 5 pictures; the third-person body wears the same. The window waited 3 to 8 frames for the parts each time. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build. |

| LAVA-NO-DAMAGE-63 | Lava does no damage and is not drawn in the Red Mountain lava pool | high | v0.0.63 | open | - | - | - | Cause found in the v0.0.63 release check, round two: the check reached the Red Mountain pool with a coordinate teleport whose height was the lava surface. The teleport took that height as the player's centre, so the standing box began inside the lava bed (the solid slab under the shallow liquid), stepped down out of the slab's underside and landed on the basin floor 636 units under the lava, outside the liquid: no damage, and the view showed the bed from below. Walking into the pool from its rim stands on the bed inside the lava. Fix (v0.0.64): the height of a coordinate teleport names the floor (the feet), as the console help says, so the search starts just above it. Waits for the in-game check in the next dev build. |

| [MWSCRIPT-PLACE-NO-MODEL-62](bugs/MWSCRIPT-PLACE-NO-MODEL-62.md) | A script cannot place an NPC or a creature whose record has no placed reference in Vvardenfell | medium | v0.0.62-dev1 (branch v0.0.62-place from 7a521203 (v0.0.62-dev1 line)) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.62 (found with MWSCRIPT-PLACE-OBJECTS-62). A placed NPC or creature is spawned from a template: a reference of the same record placed in Morrowind.esm (its room map's entity) or the actor table's base of the record. A record placed nowhere in Vvardenfell has no converted model, so its Place calls stay "not yet". Planned: the builder converts each record the scripts' Place calls name into a spawn entry of its own (the record's model and entity text), whether or not the world places it. |

Those calls stay "not yet" and are counted in the MWScript feature tracker. |
| MWSCRIPT-POSITIONCELL-NPC-62 | A script or a dialogue answer that moves an NPC or a creature to another place (PositionCell) does nothing | medium | v0.0.61-dev2 (integration head edbddd1a (after v0.0.61-dev2)) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.62 (tracker MWSCRIPT-POSITIONCELL-ACTORS-62, found by MWSCRIPT-COVERAGE-62). The compiler kept every PositionCell of anything but the player as not yet, so an actor a script or a dialogue answer sends to another cell stayed where it was. Carried out with the rules of OpenMW 0.51 OpPositionCell: the destination worked out at build time, the move kept on the world change list by the actor's reference (so it holds after leaving and coming back and after a save and a load), the actor left out at its home and spawned in the room it was sent to when that room loads. The same work carries out AIFollowCell, AIEscort and AIEscortCell (OpenMW aifollow.cpp, aiescort.cpp): the player's followers within 800 units now go through doors, travel and region loads with the player, an escort leads the player to its destination, and both are kept in saved games. The feature tracker: 409 scripts running before PositionCell, 435 after the escorts; every dialogue answer that calls PositionCell or AIFollowCell runs (7,385 of 7,411). In-game check to follow. |
| [MWSCRIPT-POSITIONCELL-OUTDOOR-62](bugs/MWSCRIPT-POSITIONCELL-OUTDOOR-62.md) | An NPC or a creature a script sends outdoors appears there only while its home area is loaded | low | v0.0.61-dev2 (integration head edbddd1a (after v0.0.61-dev2)) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.62 (found with MWSCRIPT-POSITIONCELL-NPC-62). A move into the outdoors is kept on the world change list, but the streamed outdoors spawns an actor only with the area it belongs to, so the actor stands at its new place only while its own area is loaded (moved within the loaded outdoors, it is put there at once). The same holds for a follower whose home is outdoors after a saved game is loaded in a room: it comes back once its home area loads (a follower going through a door during play comes along). Planned: a small per-area table of the actors moved into it, read when the area joins, as the rooms have. |

| NPC-BAKE-STAGES-OVERRUN-62 | The new seam and floor character bake made every stage that bakes characters run far past its history: room batches about 2 h 40 min, actor library about 40 min, player bodies 35+ min | high | v0.0.62 (2026_11_08_v0.0.62_full-v0.0.62_fe90f8e) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.62 release build. | [NPC-BAKED-WHOLE-DUPLICATION-33](bugs/NPC-BAKED-WHOLE-DUPLICATION-33.md) | Every NPC appearance is baked whole: shared body parts are converted again for each actor, and equipment cannot change | high | v0.0.32 | open | - | - | - | PERSISTING in v0.0.48-rc1 (24 October 2026): stage 1 of docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md (parts library, gallery from parts) is built; stage 2 (residents from the library) and stage 3 (the engine composed-model loader) were never built, and v0.0.48 baked the 1,769 interior residents whole, every one with its own 64 animation frames: the rc1 image carries about 1,500 MB of actor models against 297 MB for Morrowind.bsa (ROOM-RESIDENT-MODELS-SIZE-48). Stages 2 and 3 come first in v0.0.49 (docs/ROADMAP.md, "The actors get the CHIM rule"). The maintainer (2026-10-25 17:28 +0200 / 2026-10-25 15:28 UTC, TG 17:27): the whole idea is that all actors use the shared lookup table for actions; the common actions need shared lookup tables. The animations are baked per actor too: every mover holds its own walk, run and attack frames (992 MB of the 1.5 GB of actors in v0.0.51), so the region actors got no movers at all (ANIMKIT-COVERAGE-35). Wanted: one shared animation table per skeleton, the body parts as a library, each actor composed and skinned once at load (docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md stages 2-3); first measure the load-time skinning cost of one town on the 68030/68040 target. Raised to the v0.0.52 list after the door table (DOOR-ENTRANCE-AUDIT-51). Progress (2026-10-25 21:20 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:20 UTC, v0.0.52 Skeletons Of Society, method C in docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md): the shared humanoid table holds every group (139 of 139, the combat phases and the inventory poses included; walking, running, sneaking, swimming and jumping held in place); the engine reads the table and a model s skeletal block and poses it per drawn frame (aw_skel.c, r_alias.c), the protocol carries frames past 255 (U_AW_EXT AWU_FRAME2); the first real skeletal actor, a Balmora resident, is 359,184 bytes for every motion against 395,700 for today s idle-only bake (plus a mover of about 501 KB), engine pose within 0.20 model units of the baked frames at idle (the two-bone joint blend up to 1.24 units in run and death poses); box 66 x 81 x 41 units, 0 of 5,046 frames clamped. Open: SKEL-VERTEX-LIMIT-52, SKEL-TABLE-SIZE-52, the game logic for every group (ANIMKIT-COVERAGE-35), the in-game prototype and SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52. Payload plan (2026-10-25 21:34 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:34 UTC; the maintainer: the disk space is too large, it should not be in the package): skeletons alone remove the 992 MB of baked frames and the second (mover) model, but each character s mesh and skin stay stored once per character (about two thirds skin): about 1,770 characters x about 360 KB, roughly 600 MB. The parts library (each body part once, measured at about 67 MB for every resident against about 535 MB baked whole) assembled at load is the other half: v0.0.52 takes both, with a hard actor budget in the size ledger. Ship rule (2026-10-25 21:41 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:41 UTC, the maintainer: would that include the 990 MB of prebaked frames in the game? No): from v0.0.52 a shipped build carries no baked actor frames and no mover models; the baked method is a test-build option only (the animation stage A/B, a few MB); a kit check refuses a shipped build that has them. Default (2026-10-25 21:41 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:41 UTC, the maintainer: skeletons by default, they take a fraction; whoever wants the prebaked frames compiles the game with them): --npc-anim-type 2 is the builder default; 1 only when chosen at build time. Design (2026-10-25 21:58 +0200 / 2026-10-25 19:58 UTC, the maintainer: can the reused modules carry the movement; baking is impossible once actors change clothes): parts carry no motion; 479 of 519 rigid parts drawn with their one bone s matrix (Quake-style, the cost of a static model), about 40 skin parts take the joint blend; the motion is the one shared table. Movement sets per part would be per-part baking, the same mistake; a baked actor cannot change clothes without a bake per outfit. docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md Getting NPC movement right. Measured again (2026-10-25 23:54 +0200 / 2026-10-25 21:54 UTC, v0.0.52-dev1-try3): the boot payload is 3,028,309,475 bytes, id1/progs 1,996,183,591 of it (the baked actors and their mover models): 820 units had to move off DH0 onto the world volumes. Builder (2026-10-26 00:54 +0200 / 2026-10-25 22:54 UTC, v0.0.52, method C step C3): --npc-anim-type 1 or 2 in tools/build.py, default 2 (skeletal); 1 = the baked kit exactly as before. Type 2: every humanoid resident (prepare_area.build_resident: towns, Seyda Neen, rooms) and actor-library model (npc_library) is one rest frame on the shared table of its skeleton (progs/humanoid.awsk; progs/humanoid_f.awsk, the female groups layered over the common ones as OpenMW stacks xbase_anim_female over xbase_anim; progs/humanoid_kna.awsk, the beasts), each written once; the kit layout names the table's frames; no mover models, no baked frames; the type is in the resident stages' keys (AMIWIND_NPC_ANIM_TYPE) and the actor library's appearance keys. Size ledger (the base game's 2,612 placed NPC records, the react+full profile, files before resident sharing): type 1 3,222 MB for the 2,515 it bakes (models 1,256 MB, movers 1,957 MB), type 2 512 MB for the same 2,515 plus 1.8 MB of tables (about 1,281 KB against 204 KB an actor); docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md. Open: the in-game check, SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52, the kit check that refuses baked frames in a shipped build, the parts library (the skins and meshes per character are what is left). Kit check (2026-10-26 01:44 +0200 / 2026-10-25 23:44 UTC): the release guard (the kit tooling) refuses a v0.0.52-or-later release whose image build does not record npc_anim_type 2 (build-state.json, written by tools/build.py since 471cadcd): no baked actor frames in a shipped build. To confirm on the dev1-try5 build state once written. Progress (v0.0.63, 9 November 2026, IMAGE-BIGGER-THAN-ORIGINAL-62): the whole-baked actor models now share their texture coordinates and triangles (about 78 MB less, in v0.0.63-dev1); their skins can be stored as shared 16x16 tiles (builder option --skin-tiles, experimental, off by default: about 319 MB less on the v0.0.63-dev1 payload, its load time on the Pi 4B to be measured first). |

| [NPC-LIBRARY-NO-UNIT-CACHE-63](bugs/NPC-LIBRARY-NO-UNIT-CACHE-63.md) | The NPC appearance bakes of the actor library stage had no unit cache, so every rebuild of the stage baked all 418 appearances again (about 45 minutes) | critical | v0.0.63-dev1 (2026_11_09_v0.0.63-dev1_full-v0.0.63-dev1_dc356e3) | open | - | - | - | REGRESSED in v0.0.64-dev2 (fixed in v0.0.63 before): The v0.0.64-dev2 build (d031c7b5, reusing the dev1 run) took 0 of 418 NPC appearances and 0 of 48 creature models from their unit caches and baked them all, about 20 minutes; the dev1 build had taken 418 of 418 from the cache. A change merged between them (the trap rows in the script actor tables, or the cache key changes for the expansion layers) is inside the unit key's reach.. Before: The v0.0.63-dev1 build refused to reuse the actor library stage because stages it reads (the CHIM towns and the census) ran again with different outputs, and the stage then baked every NPC appearance and creature again. The reuse plan before the build had listed the stage as reused, since it cannot know that those outputs will differ. Fix in progress on the v0.0.63 line: each appearance and each creature model is kept in the unit cache the moment it is baked, keyed on its own records and parts, the bake code it runs and the settings that code reads; and the reuse plan marks a stage whose inputs are rebuilt as at risk. |

| PHOTO-CROSSHAIR-51 | In photo mode the crosshair stays: crosshair off and dbg crosshair off do nothing, and photo mode does not hide it by itself | low | v0.0.51 (2026_10_25_v0.0.51_final_d74cc652) | open | - | - | - | Open: the maintainer on TG (2026-10-25 16:39 +0200 / 2026-10-25 14:39 UTC): neither crosshair off nor dbg crosshair off works in photo mode, which should turn the crosshair off by default anyway. Next: read the photo mode draw path and the crosshair cvar in the engine. The maintainer (2026-10-25 16:45 +0200 / 2026-10-25 14:45 UTC, TG 16:41-16:44): the crosshair is fundamentally broken in v0.0.51, Options crosshair menu and type changes included (OPTIONS-CROSSHAIR-STYLE-48 reopened). Wanted: the F10 console crosshair on/off overrides the Options setting and updates the Options menu with it; photo mode hides the crosshair by default. The maintainer (2026-10-25 16:52 +0200 / 2026-10-25 14:52 UTC, TG 16:48): the crosshair also stays in the vanity camera (the idle orbit camera around the player), where it should disappear. Cause found (2026-10-25 17:09 +0200 / 2026-10-25 15:09 UTC, the maintainer TG 17:07: the crosshair vanished while switching dbg hud on and off): every shot was taken in inspect mode (dbg hud on: INSPECT click pin / right exit), and engine/aga/src/view.c V_RenderView draws the inspect centre mark '+' whenever inspect is on, regardless of the crosshair cvar, photo mode, the orbit camera or the chase camera, and with it the player crosshair is skipped (pick 2), so Options shape and colour changes never show. Fix: the inspect mark obeys the same rules (off in photo mode, in the vanity and chase cameras, with crosshair 0 and with the HUD hidden) and the player crosshair style stays in charge outside inspect. |

| PLACED-PIT-AXE-NO-FOCUS-61 | The iron shardaxe in the Seyda Neen pit is drawn but shows no item box and cannot be taken | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61 (tracker WORLD-OBJECT-PLACEMENT-59). The items index lists the iron shardaxe, unowned, in Seyda Neen (-2, -10) at -13088 -74893 102, and the game draws it there, but no item box shows and E takes nothing. Cause, measured in game with aw_placed aim (a check command that prints what the aim test makes of each row near the eye): the axe lies in a dip, about 40 map units below the eye, and its origin is under the ground surface: the line of sight from the eye to the origin stops 8.3 to 8.4 map units short of it (the test allows 6), even with the crosshair 0.8 units from it at 27 units. The aim test only looked at the item's origin: how near the view line passes it (4 map units) and whether the origin itself can be seen; a long item lying with its origin at one end, or sunk into the ground, could not be aimed at. Fix on the v0.0.61 line: a row the placed list draws is aimed at where the view ray enters its model's box, turned and scaled as it is drawn, at the distance of that point, and the line of sight is tested to that point, as the original and OpenMW 0.51 test the activation ray against the object itself; rows the map draws itself keep the origin test. Native tests in tests/aga_focus_pickup_test.c. Checked in game on the v0.0.61-dev1 image with the fixed engine (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast), from 47 game units south of the axe: the ray meets the axe's model at 36.8 map units with the view pitched down 80 degrees, the box shows "Iron Shardaxe, Weight: 30, Value: 100" with E: Take, and E takes it (the world change list counts it taken; the axe is gone from the spot). The gold coin nearby, which the ray misses, is still aimed at and taken through the origin test. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build. |

| PLAYER-FORTIFY-END-AS-DAMAGE-61 | When a Fortify Attribute effect on the player ends, the character sheet keeps it as a raised modifier and records the drop as damage | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61. The sheet keeps one modifier per attribute (the race and birthsign fortify) and a damage value. A Fortify Attribute on the player raises the modifier; when it ends, the lower value is stored as damage instead of lowering the modifier again. The shown attribute is right, but the damage can be restored by a Restore Attribute effect, which leaves the attribute raised for good. Worn Constant Effect items that fortify an attribute make it happen at every change of gear. Planned: the effects' share of the modifier kept apart from the sheet's own. |

| RESIST-NORMAL-WEAPONS-61 | Ghosts and other creatures that resist normal weapons take full damage from ordinary weapons, with no "no effect" message | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Shipped in v0.0.61 (the rule, the weapon flags, the message box), but a real ghost still took full damage there: the resistance was read from the active effect list only, which holds cast spells and worn items, never a creature's own abilities. Fixed in source for v0.0.62 (branch v0.0.62-combat): the target's resistance now also sums the spells of its own list that act always (abilities, blights, diseases and curses; OpenMW 0.51 activespells.cpp), which gives the "immune to normal weapons" ability of 68 creatures and one NPC of the game data, the vampires' 50 % and a few named abilities; the answer is kept per actor so a fight reads the list once. Host-tested (tests/test_actorstate.py). Left: the in-game check on an image with the change (an ancestor ghost: an iron weapon has no effect and the box shows, a silver one hurts; dbg combat dice off makes every swing land for a low-skill character, whose hit chance against a ghost is 0 by the original formula). |
| REST-CENSUS-NO-CELL-ID-61 | The rest window offers Rest in the Census and Excise Office, a cell the game marks as no sleeping | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61 (tracker REST-WAIT-59). The game data marks the Census and Excise Office as a cell where sleeping is not allowed, but in the office the T window opens in Rest mode, and a rest there brings the level-up box; dbg cell there answers that the map has no cell number. Cause: the map does carry its cell keys (_aw_cell_int 763 and its cell ID), but the reader of the map's world entity that dbg cell, the debug HUD and the rest window share stopped at the first value longer than 127 bytes. The compiled rooms (the Census and Excise Office, the Imperial Prison Ship) carry their light grid rows, about 980 bytes each, before the cell keys, so both read as rooms without a cell. CHIM rooms carry no light grid there and were read right. Fix on the v0.0.61 line: a long value is read to its end and kept cut, so the keys after it are found; native test tests/aga_hud_test.c with light grid rows before the keys. Checked in game on the v0.0.61-dev1 image with the fixed engine: dbg cell in the office answers INT 763, "Seyda Neen, Census and Excise Office", and T opens the window with the game line that resting here is illegal and Enter: Wait. Fixed once it ships in a numbered build. |

| [ROOM-DECAL-ALPHA-62](bugs/ROOM-DECAL-ALPHA-62.md) | A cobweb compiled into a room is drawn as a solid dark sheet instead of see-through | medium | v0.0.61 | open | - | - | - | 2026-11-10, branch v0.0.64-fence2: the renderer now has a see-through face kind. The converter marks every texture whose alpha channel leaves at least 1 % of its texels under half alpha (name prefix "{", palette index 255 for its transparent texels; other textures keep their bytes and unit keys), and the engine draws those faces in a separate pass after the walls, z-tested, skipping index 255 (aw_fence, dbg fence; off by default until a measured A/B on the next full build decides). Proof pending: the cobweb in Andrano Ancestral Tomb and a hanging growth outdoors with the switch off and on. Earlier: Open, PERSISTING (reported on the v0.0.61 release image and again in v0.0.62-dev1). The cobweb in the Andrano Ancestral Tomb is drawn as an opaque plane with no transparency, and the hanging growths under the giant mushrooms and trees outdoors also draw as solid rectangles. The whole alpha path for planes and decals is suspect, indoors and outdoors alike: every alpha-tested texture in rooms and in the open world is to be checked, not only the cobweb, and fixed for every see-through surface of the game. Wider title for the work: alpha-tested planes and decals draw opaque, indoors and outdoors (tracker ROOM-DECAL-ALPHA-62). |

| [ROOM-LOAD-KEEPS-EXTERIOR-CACHE-64](bugs/ROOM-LOAD-KEEPS-EXTERIOR-CACHE-64.md) | Entering a large room from a town keeps the town's CHIM model cache, so the room can run out of Fast RAM at 32 MB although it fits on its own | high | v0.0.64-dev2 (MiniWind v0.0.64-dev2 akulakhan-chamber try3) | open | - | - | - | Corrected 10 November 2026 after reading the room grow (chim_world.c Chim_RoomGrow, chim_room.c RoomPreGrow): the 3,888,880 bytes of "cache" in the heap line are the Quake cache inside the Hunk gap, which the room's Hunk allocations evict; and the town's 6 MiB CHIM model bank is already counted in what the zone and banks give (12,775 KiB at the first try). What is short is Fast RAM outside the Hunk: 12 MiB were free at boot, 6 MiB went to the CHIM bank, and after Balmora only 3,011 KiB are free when the room asks (74 KiB given back by the re-makeable releasers; 492 KiB on the second try). So about 3 MB of Fast RAM stays with something Balmora loaded. The room's Hunk step takes 2,012 KiB (the zone, chim_reserve_kib 2,048 KiB and 1,553 KiB for the map's rest take the remainder); with the 3 MB the room would fit. Next: a per-owner count of the Fast RAM in use before and after the map change (aw_memcensus), then give the holder back at a room load or make it re-makeable. |

| SKEL-RUNTIME-COST-52 | The skeletal prototype poses every vertex twice a drawn frame, with three divisions and three float-to-integer conversions each: it must cost what a baked frame costs | high | v0.0.52-dev1 (v0.0.52-dev-source-92f2e8ac) | open | - | - | - | Open (method C, docs/MODULAR_NPCS.md): the first working version poses an actor s vertices into a scratch frame (bone matrix, quantised with three divisions and three float-to-integer conversions, which the 68040 has no hardware instruction for) and the alias path then transforms them again: about twice today s per-vertex work, every drawn frame, estimated at several ms per 1,500-vertex actor on a 25 MHz 68040 (not measured). The method itself costs what baked frames cost: (1) fold each bone s matrix into the one per-vertex transform (view x model x bone, the light direction turned into each bone s space once), so each vertex is transformed once, no divisions or conversions; (2) pose an actor only when its frame changes (alias frames change about 10 times a second, drawn frames 20 to 30); (3) actors on the same table frame share the bone pose; (4) far actors pose less often and skip the joint blend. Acceptance: the frame time of the MiniWind animation stage (SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52) and of CHIM Balmora on the slow-CPU preset no worse than with today s baked actors. Render plan (2026-10-25 22:11 +0200 / 2026-10-25 20:11 UTC, after reading AmiQuake s r_alias.c and r_main.c): the actor stays one entity (one box, one light sample, one dynamic light pass, the existing triangle drawing); per bone one combined view x model x bone matrix and the light direction in bone space; the builder sorts vertices by bone so the inner loop keeps one matrix per run (a rigid vertex = a baked vertex s work); pose only on a table-frame change (about 8 a second, a few thousand float operations per actor a second); per-frame ready-made matrices would cost 1.9 to 3.8 MB for the common table and are not worth it; blending between table frames can be switched off (nearest frame). A part that looks wrong rigid and costs too much blended may keep a small shared baked deformation, measured. Progress (2026-10-25 23:46 +0200 / 2026-10-25 21:46 UTC): (1) r_alias.c keeps posed frames (8 slots, least recently drawn out; key model, header place, table frame): an actor is posed only when its table frame changes (about 8 a second against 20 to 30 draws) and actors of one model on one frame share the pose; every other draw is a baked frame's work. (2) AW_SkelPoseVerts folds each bone's matrix once with the rest scale and the alias quantisation: per vertex one 3 x 4 transform per bone used, no division; the byte rounding adds 1.5 x 2^23 and reads the mantissa instead of a float-to-integer conversion (the 68040 has no FINTRZ: it traps into the emulation). Native tests within one byte of the builder; compiles for 68040 and 68060 at -O1 and -O2. Not yet measured on the slow-CPU preset (the animation stage). Measured (2026-10-26 05:57 +0200 / 2026-10-26 03:57 UTC, SKEL-ANIM-STAGE-52): the same MiniWind stage built twice from 7064ea39, --npc-anim-type 1 (baked) and 2 (skeletal). Both ran on the slow-CPU preset (FS-UAE cycle-exact 68040 at x14, 49.7 MHz), 32 MB Fast RAM, the Balmora arrival pose at 09:09 with the residents in their own idle (no stage), aw_rcount 2, 15 one-second lines each. Baked: alias 25.7 ms median (25.6 to 26.0) for 2 alias models drawn, view 1,134 ms, frame 1,261 ms. Skeletal: alias 33.7 ms median (33.5 to 76.0) for 3 alias models drawn, view 1,142 ms, frame 1,271 ms; the 4 lines at about 76 ms are the seconds in which the residents' idle stepped to a new table frame (posing). Per drawn model that is 12.8 ms baked against 11.2 ms skeletal when drawn from the pose cache and about 25 ms when posed. The whole frame was 9 ms (0.7 %) slower at the median and up to 57 ms (4.5 %) slower when posing. Not like for like in one respect: the skeletal build drew one more alias model at this pose (al 3 against 2). Acceptance not met yet: posing costs about twice a baked frame per model. The animated stage (8 actors cycling) on the slow preset is not measured yet. Profiled and cut (2026-10-26 09:57 +0200 / 2026-10-26 07:57 UTC). Setup: dbg rcount times the posing (b16bb912: RT_SKELPOSE and RT_SKELVERTS inside the alias time, the kp field with poses made and pose-cache hits), slow-CPU preset (FS-UAE cycle-exact 68040 x14), 32 MB, Balmora arrival pose, residents idle, aw_rcount 2, 15 one-second lines each. Before (b16bb912): one pose was 0.80 ms of bones (AW_SkelPose) and 13.2 ms of vertices (AW_SkelPoseVerts), about 14 ms in all; the vertices are 94 % of it. 871d87e6: a whole frame takes its one key with no blend, square root or division; the never-moving bones are made once per table; the vertex loop has its transforms written out on direct i16 reads. A pose is now 0.61 ms of bones and 9.5 ms of vertices (-28 %). Also fixed there: a forced animation stood still on a slow machine (frames over 0.5 s gave dt 0). 38d6c751: 32 posed frames when AW_TryMalloc allows (the 8 kept slots at 16 MB), so idle residents (an 8-frame loop) stop posing after their first loop. Like for like on one HEAD (3715e8c4), the same pose: baked (--npc-anim-type 1) alias 25.7 ms median, frame 1,272 ms; skeletal alias 33.2 ms, frame 1,275 ms (+0.2 %), with 0 poses in every sampled second. The skeletal side drew 3 alias models against 2 (the extra one passes the cull, likely on the skeletal model's larger box: nothing more is visible in the stills), so per drawn model it is 11.1 ms skeletal against 12.8 ms baked. Worst case, the stage with 8 actors changing group every frame: 8 poses a frame at 0.62 + 8.8 ms each, alias 293 ms against 216 ms held, frame 1.73 s against 1.64 s (+5.6 %). Open: the skeletal box that admits an off-screen actor, and the posing itself (vertices about 8.8 ms a pose on the slow preset). Cull box fixed and remeasured. 685fb2f3 (gate 4031) culls a skeletal actor by the box of the pose it stands in: each posed frame in the pose cache keeps its vertices' box, and the cull uses it once the frame has been posed (before that, the rest frame's every-pose box). Like for like, slow-CPU preset, 32 MB, Balmora arrival pose, residents idle, 15 lines each. Skeletal (stage build 685fb2f3): 2 alias models drawn (the same as baked), alias 25.1 ms median, frame 1,261 ms (one line at 2.2 s), 0 poses and 2 pose-cache hits a second. Baked (3715e8c4, --npc-anim-type 1): 2 models, alias 25.7 ms, frame 1,272 ms. Skeletal is now no slower than baked at this pose (alias -2 %, frame -0.9 %). Open: only the worst case, 8 actors changing group every frame (+5.6 %, about 8.8 ms of vertices a pose). |

| [SMOKE-STALL-LABEL-INFERRED-60](bugs/SMOKE-STALL-LABEL-INFERRED-60.md) | The boot smoke names a stop an emulator disk stall without checking the pending disk request | medium | v0.0.60 | open | - | - | - | Open. classify() names a stop emulator-disk when every PC sample is in Kickstart's idle loop, the game waits on SIGF_DOS and a word on the game's stack equals another process's message-list address. The label is inferred: a stack word can be a stale pointer from an earlier call, and the active DOS packet, its owner and any pending device request are not checked. What the check establishes is a guest DOS wait with the completion layer unresolved. Next: name it that way, or add the host-side checks (the emulator's queued replies and its interrupt-request flag) to the stall examination; count only confirmed captures against CHIM-SEYDA-BALMORA-LOAD-HANG-43. |

| [UNDERWATER-BREATH-62](bugs/UNDERWATER-BREATH-62.md) | Underwater there is no breath meter and no drowning, and Water Breathing is not applied | high | v0.0.62-dev1 | open | - | - | - | v0.0.63 release check, round two: an Argonian read Water Breathing 0 at the start, after a load and after a teleport, and drowned in the Seyda Neen bay. Cause found: in the original game data the Argonian race spell "argonian breathing" is a castable spell (Water Breathing for 120 s on self, always succeeds), not a constant ability; OpenMW gives the race's spells to the player's spell list the same way, and a castable spell works only when it is cast. Water Breathing 0 before casting it is therefore the original behaviour; the check expected a constant effect. The engine keeps the spell in the list (character creation, a race change, a loaded game: fix fb279aeb). The in-game check is now: the player knows the spell, casts it, reads Water Breathing 1 for 120 s and does not drown. Cause found in v0.0.64 (round three): the console's sorted id lookup treated a successful read of the actor table as a failure, so player->getspell answered 0 for every spell, also for a player holding the race power; fixed in the engine (the read is checked the right way round), with a test of every call site. |

| WEAPON-STRIKE-ENCHANT-NOT-CAST-61 | A weapon's Cast When Strikes enchantment is not cast when the weapon hits | medium | v0.0.61-dev1 (2026_11_05_v0.0.61-dev1_full-v0.0.61-dev1_374d59b) | open | - | - | - | Open, v0.0.61, fixed on the v0.0.61-magicitems line, waiting for a numbered build. The builder writes every enchantment of the masters into the actor table and links the shared items to theirs; a weapon blow that hits or is blocked casts the weapon's Cast When Strikes enchantment on the one struck, the killing blow too, with its charge by the Enchant skill (the player's weapon and an NPC's, by OpenMW 0.51 combat.cpp applyOnStrikeEnchantment). Seen in game on a MiniWind Seyda Neen image (FS-UAE, 32 MB Fast): the iron shardaxe's Frost Damage landed on Fargoth three times, its charge fell 10 -> 9 -> 8 -> 7 and recharged slowly, the fight started; a missed swing cast nothing. | WORLD-BUTTONS-62 | Buttons and levers that should act do nothing, for example the Ghostgate gate buttons on both sides | high | v0.0.62-dev1 | open | - | - | - | v0.0.63 release check, round two: the console answered "no such reference here" for the Ghostgate switches and portcullises. Cause: the console looked its target up among the entities only, and the CHIM world keeps these objects as placements without an entity (their scripts run as attached instances, the portcullises move through the door table), so a console line could not name them; the player's own use (E) was not affected. Fix (v0.0.64): the console also finds a placement by the scripts' object table: an attached script instance of that id (the nearest one for an id placed more than once) or a scripted mover, with its position (a mover's where it stands now); Activate from the console is the player's use, so the object's own OnActivate script takes it. Waits for the in-game check in the next dev build. |
| WORLD-OBJECT-STATE-NOT-SAVED-59 | World objects taken or moved are not remembered: they come back when the cell or room reloads, and saves do not keep them | high | v0.0.59-dev2 | open | - | - | - | Objects part fixed in v0.0.59 (CELL-CHANGES-59, first slice): one sorted change list for the whole world keyed by a stable reference id (content file and reference number), only changed fields (taken, disabled, lock, stolen mark, moved position, drops), an index by cell, room and scene for map load, no 1,024 or 32 ceiling, kept for the session and saved. Verified at 32 MB Fast on a Seyda Neen MiniWind: an item taken in Arrille's Tradehouse stays taken after another map and after a quicksave and quickload; an item taken outdoors in Seyda Neen stays taken after another map; a bottle dropped outdoors lies there after another map and after a load. Doors, locks and the stolen mark fixed in v0.0.59 (second slice): a hinged door left open stands open when its room or frame comes back and after a load (the census hall door's own saved pose folded in); a lock or unlock by a script, by the console or by the player's key is kept the same way; an owned item taken is recorded as stolen from its owner (the placement's owner, else its faction) by item and owner, so the mark stays with the item through drops, map changes and saves (gold is never marked). Verified at 32 MB Fast on a Seyda Neen MiniWind: the Arrille's Tradehouse door unlocked and opened stays unlocked and open after Seyda Neen and back and after a quicksave and quickload; a Seyda Neen door locked at 75 stays locked at 75 after another map and a load; two items taken from Elone stay marked stolen from her after another map and a load. Container contents fixed in v0.0.59 (third slice): what is taken out of or put into a placed container is kept per container as the difference against its game-data contents, on the same list, kept for the session and saved; taking from an owned container is theft; a script's AddItem, RemoveItem and GetItemCount on a container use the same entries. Verified at 32 MB Fast on a Seyda Neen MiniWind: 4 of the 10 gold taken from the owned Small Chest in Arrille's Tradehouse stay taken after Seyda Neen and back and after a quicksave and quickload; an iron dagger put into the same chest stays there the same way. Still open: no in-game action moves an object yet (the field is saved and read by the placed items), no container window yet (the console's aw_placed container takes and puts), respawning containers and levelled lists inside containers, and the later slices of CELL-CHANGES-59. |

### Bugs by family

Every bug from v0.0.30 on belongs to one family (bugs with a shared cause or area); the families and their shared rules are in [bug tracking](bugs/README.md#families).

#### FPU and CPU behaviour (68040/68060) (`fpu-cpu`)

- DAGOTH-CHAMBER-JIT-FAULT-53: Loading Akulakhan's Chamber freezes with the JIT on and loads fine with the JIT off (open, high)
- [ENGINE-060-FSCC-41](bugs/ENGINE-060-FSCC-41.md): The engine has 263 fscc instructions (float comparisons as true/false), which the 68060 traps to its support library (open, medium)
- [ENGINE-060-MUL64-41](bugs/ENGINE-060-MUL64-41.md): The 68040 engine has 151 64-bit MULS.L/MULU.L instructions (divisions by constants), which the 68060 traps to its support library (open, medium)
- [ENGINE-FLOAT-SHORT-STORE-33](bugs/ENGINE-FLOAT-SHORT-STORE-33.md): 68040 engine build stored float-to-short conversions of the animation layout parser into the wrong group (open, medium)
- [ENGINE-FPSP-MISSING-31](bugs/ENGINE-FPSP-MISSING-31.md): Boot disk loads no 68040 FPU support library; emulator hides it (open, critical)
- [ENGINE-FPU-UNIMPL-31](bugs/ENGINE-FPU-UNIMPL-31.md): Every-frame math traps on a real 68040 (sin+cos become cexp) (open, high)
- [EXTENTS-FPU-RULE-31](bugs/EXTENTS-FPU-RULE-31.md): Surface extents and lightmap sizes depended on the FPU's arithmetic (open, high)
- [FPU-SUPPORT-MMULIB-SETPATCH-41](bugs/FPU-SUPPORT-MMULIB-SETPATCH-41.md): The MMULib 68060.library stops the boot with an alert on the AmiWind boot disk, which runs no SetPatch (open, high)
- [ENGINE-FPU-DATA-DECODE-33](bugs/ENGINE-FPU-DATA-DECODE-33.md): The 68040 FPU check reads a pointer table in the engine code section as fintrz instructions (fixed, medium)
- ENGINE-FPU-JUMP-TABLE-DECODE-63: The engine build's FPU check reads a switch's jump table as FPU instructions (fixed, medium)
- [ENGINE-FRAME-TIME-FLOAT-35](bugs/ENGINE-FRAME-TIME-FLOAT-35.md): The main loop held the seconds since start in floats: frame times quantise after hours of play (fixed, medium)
- [ENGINE-GAMMA-POW-35](bugs/ENGINE-GAMMA-POW-35.md): The gamma table called the C library pow, which executes FPU instructions a 68040 does not implement (fixed, low)
- COMBAT-PLAYGROUND-JIT-FREEZE-54: The combat playground freezes about 4 s into the fight of a group of four with the JIT on (closed, high)
